1.note: The edition points נָסְעוֹ "his setting out". Read as the sick man's: he will be well before the company moves on. "Before one sets out" is also possible.

2.note: These three lines are a jingle of rhyming participles (מאמירו וממאירו, משירו ומסירו, מעירו ומבעירו). "Exalts" follows Deut 26:18 הֶאֱמִירְךָ; מַמְאִיר is "stinging, malignant" (Ezek 28:24, Lev 13:51). Whether "He" is God or the charmer is not clear; the sense is uncertain.

3.note: צִירֵי can be "pangs" (Isa 21:3) or "envoys" (Prov 13:17): "envoys of plagues" is also possible.

4.note: Isa 66:6 "a voice of uproar from the city". The next line repeats מֵעִיר as "wakes" (from עור): a rhyme on the same word in two senses.

5.note: הֲדוֹם is "footstool". "Sit at his footstool" is read as "stay where he is", parallel to the next line (Exod 16:29).

6.note: The edition prints יָדַעְניּ, an odd form. The context ("we saw") calls for יָדַעְנוּ "we knew", which the translation follows.

7.note: חֵמָה is both "venom" (Deut 32:24, Ps 58:5) and "wrath"; "wrath poured out" is the phrase of Ezek 20:33. "Sucked out" (וַיָּמָץ) recalls Judg 6:38.

8.note: מַעֲרָכָה is a battle line (1 Sam 17:8); here it plays on מְעָרָה, the cave the snake lay in.

9.he: אֲנִי חֶבֶר וְחָבֵר לַחֲבֵרִים / וְלִנְחָשִׁים אֲנִי חוֹבֵר חֲבָרִים
9.note: A pun on the root חבר: Ḥever (the hero's name), "companion", and חוֹבֵר חֲבָרִים "charmer of charms" (Ps 58:6; Deut 18:11 חֹבֵר חָבֶר).
